# Chapter 1 — Scientific Infographic Storyboard
**Working design guidance; not an amendment to frozen thesis text.**  
**Deck context:** 16 editable slides = title + outline + 11 Chapter 1 sections + 3 bibliography slides. Keep frozen title and GO/SO1–SO3 word-for-word. In-text author–date source notes mandatory for externally sourced domain claims.

| Slide | Scientific question | Preferred original figure family | Essential scientific requirements | Status and QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Title | What is the research identity? | minimal two-system identity | P and the complete T_e are distinct; no “verified” two-way thermal symbol | internal canonical title and scope |
| 2. Outline | How will the argument unfold? | linear research-story roadmap | logical chapter flow, not causal physics | thesis-defined |
| 3. Background | What physically exists and connects? | side-by-side nested system boundaries + electrical exchange | external P, full T_e, non-thermal electrical transfer labeled; no automatic thermal coupling | add source-specific adjacent citations |
| 4. Research context | What does heat change independently? | top hazard + **two parallel** heat→state→capability lanes | hazard OUTSIDE both systems; no cross-system heat arrow | transformer and charger citations each adjacent |
| 5. Research problem | What qualifies a thermal interdependency? | **two distinct candidate directional lanes**, each with evidence gate | P→T_e and T_e→P independently; source, constraint, interface, receiver, timing, service | CANDIDATE/PARTLY SUPPORTED/OPEN as admissible |
| 6. Literature/gap | Which links are established and missing? | source-by-claim matrix + bounded unresolved handoff | prior work covers transformer effects **and** some service disruptions; extreme-heat device specifics; no “first” | specific citations in evidence cells |

| 10. Approach | What will be done and tested? | gated evidence→qualification→model→verification→validation/UQ→service workflow | modeling verification ≠ empirical validation; blocked evidence stays OPEN | cited VVUQ sources |

## Arrow evidence protocol for Chapter 1
- **Physical semantics** from `scientific-diagram-design`: solid physical transfer, heavy justified causal effect, dashed control, dotted observation, thin association.
- **Evidence status** displayed separately as a word (`ESTABLISHED`, `CANDIDATE`, `OPEN`); do **not** overload dashed arrows to mean uncertainty.
- For Slide 3, use an explicitly labeled electrical-power-transfer interface and conditional bidirectional power where supported; do not infer bidirectional *thermal* mechanisms.
- For Slide 4, only heat→state→capability pathways; **no P↔T_e coupling arrow**.
- For Slide 5, two mechanism lanes are *candidate research constructs*; no quantified threshold, curve, or timing unless admitted by evidence.
- For Slide 9, say **System Boundary**, never use “Boundary condition” to classify membership.

## Mandatory demonstration tests
A) Given shared extreme heat, a successful diagram shows two independent response lanes and no automatic dependency.  
B) Given a candidate charger derating mechanism, a successful diagram requires AC-grid input behavior before inferring transformer thermal response.  
C) Given a selected fast-charger use case, a successful diagram retains the full T_e canonical scope and labels the selected case as a modeling subset.

Design only; no new scientific result, equipment choice, or model parameter is authorized by this storyboard.
